rationales.1: The no-motion render carries all three steps' full qualified copy and a complete spec table, but the resolved plan-sheet drawing sits only beside Step 1, leaving Steps 2 and 3 without their own visual companion in the static layout.
rationales.2: The hero headline and subhead name the product, its audience, and the folded/unfolded numbers directly, readable before any scroll.
rationales.3: All three flagged figures (n=14 median setup, estimated pack volume, certification-pending load rating) carry their qualifiers verbatim in the dimensions table, and price/trial terms are plain.
rationales.4: Skip control is clearly labeled and sized in the header and the gates confirm native scroll with no rewrite; nothing in the captures suggests hunting is required.
rationales.5: The technical-drawing register, label typography, and rust accent stay coherent across both themes and viewports, giving a restrained, confident system.
rationales.6: Best-in-set LCP (280/440ms) and interaction latency (32/64ms) in the measured data; desktop frame-time p95 (16.8ms) sits a hair over the 16.7ms line, a trivial but real miss shared with the other candidates.
rationales.7: The plan sheet literally resolving from a bag outline into hull line-work most directly stages the bag-to-hull transformation the brief asks for, though a static capture can't confirm how the water beat pays off in motion.
rationales.8: Both declared breaks (no product shot; dimensions as drawing callouts) are visible, but a fully conventional 'Dimensions and materials' spec table also appears later on the page, in tension with the declared 'not as a spec table' break.
rationales.9: Copy stays plain and boat-specific ('lives under your bed,' 'six creases, one tension lever') without launch-page hype-idiom.
rationales.10: The second-visit gate confirms an instant static return with price visible, though reaching it still means passing the full three-step narrative section first.
